Creating an icon is not an easy task for a designer
Because an icon must be universal, it can be very tricky for a designer to create
a workable icon. There are so many things to take into consideration. For example,
a representation  of something could be  interpreted  differently depending on
someone’s culture, beliefs or religion. Colors might also need to be avoided. In
Europe, red is a common symbol for danger, but in China, red symbolizes good
fortune and is believed to keep away evil.
Some words are considered impossible to translate into a pictogram without the
help of text. Try to represent an ‘account manager’ as an icon for example. It might
not seem too hard at first, but when you think about it, you’ll soon realize that it’s
not an easy task at  all.
It’s also very risky to try to do something differently when creating a new icon.
If a triangle in a circle means play, don’t try to reinvent the wheel.  It’ll simply
confuse people. Icons are not always the place to be creative.
Are some of the existing icons  still up to date today?
When you look at some of today’s most popular icons, a question may pop into
your head: “How long are we going to keep these without updating them?” This
question applies particularly to technology, which is constantly evolving year after
year. Electronic devices become smaller, thinner, able to perform two or more tasks
simultaneously and equipped with touch screens. Their shapes are also changing,
as well as the way we are using them.
Is this icon  still correctly understood today?
Generation Z was born with tablets and smart phones, so can they really identify
the old-fashioned phone receiver we use to represent calls? Are they aware that
the voicemail icon is actually a tape recorder? Do they actually know what a tape
recorder is? Those are the kinds of questions to bring up when looking at smart
phones or computers. It seems that those types of icons have become ideograms
instead  of  pictograms, as they seem  to be symbols  that have  finally been
universally accepted as the official representation of an idea or concept.

A SWOT analysis is a framework and a diagnostic tool that is used to help you
understand the external and internal factors which can influence a project or an
organisation. The name is an acronym for the four elements of a SWOT analysis
which are:
1. Strengths: These are positive contributions that have happened during the
timescale of an activity/project that should be celebrated. This would include any
advantages to the organisation such as upskilling, reputation, resources etc...,
2. Weaknesses: These are activities or areas that have been identified could be
improved such as any gaps, inefficiencies etc...,
3. Opportunities: These offer any opportunities for improvement that will contribute
to strengthening your project or organisation that you could take advantage of,
4. Threats: These are external factors that can negatively affect the performance
or survival of project. External means that they are usually outside of the
departments or organisations control.
Strengths and Weaknesses are seen as intrinsic within a project or organisation
whereas Opportunities and Threats are seen as extrinsic factors that occur outside
of the organisations control. A SWOT analysis allows you to generate information
so that you can evaluate the current situation, identifying areas to improve and
grow and address any challenges in achieving goals that have been created for a
project or organisation.

Ⅴ. 심화 영어Ⅰ 성취수준
예시 답안
Hello, everyone. Today, I’d like to introduce our app redesign project. The app we
selected is called AAATalk. It is a messaging app mostly used by teenagers, and it
allows users to chat and share pictures quickly and easily.
Let’s begin by looking at the original icon.  It currently is a blue paper envelope
placed with a square background. This symbol was commonly used in the past to
represent sending and receiving more formal written messages, similar to email.
However, for most teenagers today, that symbol no longer feels familiar or relevant.
It looks outdated and doesn’t reflect the real–time, image–centered communication
that modern users enjoy.
Now, let’s take a look at our redesigned icon. In our version, we replaced the
envelope with a speech bubble that contains a camera symbol inside  it. We also
changed the color to bright purple, which feels more energetic, eye–catching, and
appealing to younger users.
Why did we choose these changes? First, the speech bubble is a clear and universal
symbol for live messaging, and the camera inside highlights how important photo
sharing is for today’s users. Compared to an envelope, this combination offers a more
symbolic meaning for how communication actually happens in this app. Second, the
new color choice helps the app stand out on users’ screens. Bright purple gives a
fun, friendly impression, which fits well with the app’s teenage audience.
In conclusion, we believe that a meaningful and familiar icon can make a big
difference in how users feel about an app. Our redesigned icon not only looks more
modern, but it also represents the actual way people communicate today, through
images, chatting, and fast interaction. That’s why this new design is a better fit for
AAATalk and its users.
Thank you for listening.

서술형(구술형)
담화를 듣고, ‘optimal number’의 의미와 그것이 Jane의 식당에 어떻게 적용되었는지를
<조건>에 맞게 영어로 설명하시오.   [6점]
W: I’d like to say something about the relationship between the number of waiters
and the profit in a restaurant. Let’s imagine Jane opened a restaurant with one
waiter. The food was good, but customers had to wait too long to be served.
As a result, Jane’s profits were only $4,000 per month. She decided to hire a
second waiter, which increased her profits to $6,000. A third waiter boosted
her profits to $6,500. However, when Jane hired a fourth waiter, her profits
decreased to $5,500. This shows that there is an optimal number of waiters
for a restaurant. When there are too few waiters, customers have to wait too
long and profits suffer. However, when there are too many waiters, they can
get in each other’s way and productivity decreases. As a result, profits start
to decline. The optimal number of waiters for a restaurant will vary depending
on the size of the restaurant, the type of food it serves, and the number of
customers it typically serves. However, this concept shows that there is a point
at which adding more waiters will no longer increase profits.

Ⅵ. 심화 영어Ⅱ 성취수준
2. 평가 도구
서술형
다음은 신경 가소성과 학습(neuroplasticity and learning)에 관한 글이다. 글을 읽고, 밑줄
친 the “fire together, wire together” principle이 다음 글에서 의미하는 바를 <조건>에
맞게 영어로 기술하시오. [8점]
In the past, scientists believed that the brain ceased to develop after childhood.
But recent studies indicate that the brain is able to continue growing and evolving
throughout one’s life. This is called neuroplasticity, which refers to the ability of
the brain to change and adapt in response to life experiences. Neuro refers to
neurons, the nerve cells in the brain and nervous system. Plasticity is the capacity
to be shaped and altered. The brain’s neuroplasticity allows it to reorganize neural
pathways and to create new connections at any age.
Until the age of three, a child’s brain undergoes significant change. The young
brain experiences developmental plasticity as its neurons rapidly grow branches.
Synapses, the places where neurons connect and communicate with one another,
are formed at a faster rate than at any other time. At birth, the number of
synapses  per  neuron  is  2,500,  but  by  the age two  or  three,  there  are
approximately 15,000 synapses per neuron. This amount is about twice that of the
average adult brain. As we gain new experiences, neurons that are used frequently
develop stronger connections, while those that are rarely or never used eventually
die. The unused connections are gradually eliminated throughout childhood and
adolescence, a process referred to as synaptic pruning. Through synaptic pruning,
the brain can efficiently adapt to changes in the environment.
While the brain changes a lot during early life, adult brains are still capable of
change. This ongoing plasticity can occur as a result of learning and experience.
Neuroplasticity depends on the “fire together, wire together” principle:  If certain
neurons activate simultaneously,  they’ll eventually connect. Consistent practice,
like meditating, playing a musical instrument, or learning a new language, is likely
to alter your brain by forming new neural pathways. This is why putting in effort
over an extended period of time leads to an improvement in ability.
Moreover, knowing about neuroplasticity can enhance an individual’s motivation
and learning abilities. According to a 2009 study by psychologist Richard Nisbett,
students who were informed about the brain’s capacity to change did better on

math  tests  than  those who were  not  informed.  This awareness  cultivates
confidence in learning outcomes and motivates students to persevere through
challenges. Therefore, the concept of neuroplasticity encourages us to believe in
our potential for self–growth and improvement as long as we consistently strive
for positive change.

정답 해설
Food rule은 몸에 필요하며 옳다고 여기는 기준에 따라 음식을 선택하는 것이고, Food
preference는 개인의 기호나 욕구에 따라 음식을 선택하는 것이라는 개념적 차이를 이해할 수
있다. 예를 들어 청소년 식습관 중 ‘아침 식사 거르기’인 경우 아침 식사를 거르는 것을 문제로
본 것은 food rule의 관점이고, 몸에 유익하도록 문제를 해결한다는 방향을 설정할 수 있다. 구체적
인 내용의 전개는 조건을 고려하여 첫째, ‘많은 청소년이 바쁘거나 더 자고 싶어서 아침을 거른다.’라
는 내용으로 현상을 설명하고, 둘째, ‘이는 건강과 집중력에 부정적 영향을 준다.’를 통해 문제점을
지적할 수 있다. 셋째, Food rule의 관점에서 보면, 몸에 필요한 아침 에너지를 제공해야 하는
필요성을 근거로 제시한다. 넷째, ‘아침을 거르면 피로, 집중력 저하, 간식 과다 섭취로 이어진다.’로
주장을 뒷받침할 수 있다. 따라서, 주장의 내용을 정리하여 ‘균형 잡힌 아침(탄수화물+단백질+과일)
을 먹으면 뇌 기능과 활동성이 향상된다.’를 이유로 청소년들은 아침 식사를 거르는 습관을 바꾸어
야 함을 주장하는 것이 적절하다.

예시 답안
(구술 발표)
These days, many teenagers skip breakfast because they are too busy or want to
sleep longer. However, this habit can seriously affect their health and concentration.
According to the concept of a food rule, we should eat based on what our body needs,
not just what is convenient or what others around us do. Our body needs energy in
the morning to function properly, especially during school hours. Skipping breakfast
often leads to fatigue, poor focus in class, and unhealthy snacking later in the day.
Even though some students may say they don’t feel hungry in the morning, this might
be due to habit, not actual health needs. By following a healthy food rule — such as
eating a balanced breakfast with carbohydrates, protein, and fruits — we can support
our brain function and stay more active throughout the day. Therefore, teenagers
should break the habit of skipping breakfast and make choices that respect their body’s
real needs. (158 words)

예시 답안
We chose “Social Welfare” because we believe that a truly advanced country should
take care of all of its people, not just grow its economy. Even though Korea is rich
in technology and business, many people such as the elderly and low–income families
are not receiving enough support. We think improving welfare is the key to a fair
and just society.
① Although Korea is economically developed, its social welfare spending is still below
the OECD average. Many  elderly people and low–income  individuals,  especially
those living alone, are left without proper support. The number of solitary deaths
among the elderly is increasing every year.
② The key causes include a lack of community–based welfare infrastructure, limited
public  manpower,  and  a  lack  of  social  attention  and  connection  between
generations.
③  It leads to a lower quality of  life, especially for vulnerable groups, worsening
mental health, and increasing mistrust and division between generations.  It also
weakens the people’s sense of community.
① Helsinki also faced serious elderly isolation and a shortage of caregivers due to
rapid aging.
② The city introduced the Care Service Voucher System, which allows elderly people
to choose the services they need from approved providers. This improved both
service accessibility and satisfaction through public–private cooperation.
③ Finland focuses on personal choice and  flexibility, while Korea mostly relies on
uniform, government-centered services, which can result in a mismatch between
service and actual need.

2. 평가 도구
서술형
The  following  passage  presents two  different  cases  of  competition — the
rock–paper–scissors game and a lizard’s mating behavior. Based on these cases,
explain the main idea of the passage by describing what these two cases reveal
about competition and changing strategies.
Rock–paper–scissors and Lizards
Playing games is an essential part of the human experience. Games are a safe
way of exploring real–life situations, allowing us to develop ways of predicting how,
given certain rules, events will unfold and to plan accordingly. They teach us about
chances and unpredictability, which play such essential parts in nature’s game of
life.
From ancient civilizations all around the world, we have a fascinating selection of
games: stones thrown in the sand, sticks tossed in the air, coins placed in holes
carved into wooden blocks, hands used to compete, and pictures drawn on cards.
From ancient Mancala to Monopoly, from the game of go to the poker tables of
Vegas, games are invariably won by whoever  is best at taking a mathematical,
analytical approach.
Jan–ken–pon  in  Japan,  ro–sham–bo  in  California,  kai–bai–bo  in  Korea,  and
ching–chong–cha  in South Africa — the game of rock–paper–scissors  is played  all
around the world. The rules are very simple: on a count of three, each player
makes his or her hand into one of three shapes: a fist for a rock, a flat hand for
paper, or two fingers in a V for scissors. Rock beats scissors, scissors beat paper,
and paper beats rock. Two of the same is a draw.
Now, the reason for the first two wins is clear: rock breaks the scissors, scissors
cut the paper. But why does paper beat the rock? A sheet of paper isn’t much
protection against someone throwing a rock at you. But  it may be that  this
convention goes back to ancient China, in the days when a petition to the king
was symbolized by a rock. The king would indicate whether he’d accepted the
petition by placing a piece of paper above or below the rock.  If the rock was
covered by the paper, the petition was refused and the petitioner defeated.
The origins of this game are hard to trace. There is evidence that it was played
in the Far East and by Celtic tribes, and even possibly as far back as the ancient

Egyptians, who used to play finger games. However,  all these cultures seem to
have been beaten to the discovery by a group of lizards that have been playing
the game in the fight for survival long before human beings were making fists.
The West Coast of the United States is home to a species of a lizard known as
the common side–blotched  lizard. The male comes  in three  different  colors —
orange, blue, and yellow — and each color has a different mating strategy. Orange
lizards are the strongest and will attack and beat blue lizards. The blue lizards are
bigger than the yellow lizards and are happy to engage in battle with them and
beat them. But though the yellow lizards are smaller than the blue and orange
males, they look like female lizards, and that confuses the orange lizards. So the
orange lizards, who are looking for a fight, don’t notice the yellow lizards slipping
under their gaze and mating with the females. The yellow lizards are sometimes
referred to as “sneakers” for the sneaky way in which they beat the orange ones.
So orange beats blue, blue beats yellow, and yellow beats orange — an evolutionary
version of rock–paper–scissors.
These lizards have been playing the game in the course of perpetuating their
genes for a long time, and  it would be interesting to know whether they have
developed a strategy for winning. Their population tends to follow a six-year cycle
in which first orange dominates, then yellow, then blue, then orange once again.
The pattern that emerges is precisely the one that people will use in trying to win
the game in one–to–one combat. See too many rocks being thrown and you start
to offer paper, but once your opponent sees the run of paper beating the stone,
he or she wises up and switches to scissors to cut off your paper run. You soon
pick up your opponent’s change of behavior and shift to rock.
At its heart, winning this game is all about spotting patterns, and that’s a very
mathematical  trait.  If you can predict what your opponent  is going to do next
because of a pattern of behavior he or she has established, then you’re  in. The
problem is that you don’t want there to be any immediately obvious rhythm in the
way you respond, or your opponent will gain the upper hand. A huge amount of
psychology  is going on as each contestant tries to spot patterns in his or her
opponent’s play, each second–guessing what the other might do next.

Read the two passages about culture. Then, write one paragraph that includes:
- three or more characteristics of human culture from the first passage and
- an explanation of why chimpanzee behavior can be considered cultural, using
details from the second passage.
What Is Culture?
The word culture has many different meanings. For some  it refers to an
appreciation of good literature, music, art, and food. For a biologist, it is likely
to be a colony of bacteria or other microorganisms growing in a nutrient
medium in a laboratory Petri dish. However, for anthropologists and other
behavioral scientists, culture  is the  full range of learned human behavior
patterns. The term was  first used  in  this way by the pioneer  English
anthropologist Edward B. Tylor in his book, Primitive Culture, published in
1871. Tylor said that culture is “that complex whole which includes knowledge,
belief, art, law, morals, custom, and any other capabilities and habits acquired
by man as a member of society.” Of course, it is not limited to men. Women
possess and create it as well. Since Tylor’s time, the concept of culture has
become the central focus of anthropology.
Is Culture Limited to Humans?
There is a difference of opinion in the behavioral sciences about whether
or not we are the only animal that creates and uses culture. The answer to
this question depends on how narrowly culture is defined. If it is used broadly
to refer to a complex of learned behavior patterns, then  it is clear that we
are not alone in creating and using culture. Many other animal species teach
their young what they themselves learned in order to survive. This is especially
true of chimpanzees and other relatively intelligent apes and monkeys. Wild
chimpanzee mothers typically teach their children about several hundred food
and medicinal plants. Their children also have to learn about the dominance
hierarchy and the social rules within their communities. As males become
teenagers, they acquire hunting skills from adults. Females have to learn how
to nurse and care for their babies. This kind of knowledge is not hardwired
into their brains at birth. They are all learned patterns of behavior just as they
are for humans.

논술형
Imagine you are taking on one of the following six social roles:
- A scientist
- A parent of a future child
- A patient or person with a genetic disease
- A government policy maker
- An ethicist or philosopher
- A bio-tech entrepreneur or company leader
After reading the passage provided, write a short opinion from your chosen
perspective. In your essay, explain how you view genome editing and how  it
should be handled in society. You should include what you would prioritize, what
concerns you might have, and what regulations or actions you would suggest.
Genome Editing
The dream of  precisely and accurately changing almost any part of any
genome — even in complex species such as humans — has become a reality due
to recent progress  in genome  editing. But with great power comes great
responsibility, and the ease with which this process can now be performed has
brought the ethics of genome editing to the public's attention.
Genome editing makes  it possible to change specific DNA sequences with a
great degree of control and precision, and there are abundant ways in which it
can be used, from developing new crops to improving human health. There are
a variety of techniques, but the most revolutionary involves using CRISPR, or
clustered regularly inter-spaced short palindromic repeats — parts of DNA that
work with enzymes to cut strands of DNA at specific locations.
The use of CRISPR in genome editing has prompted calls for a genome editing
moratorium from a group of concerned US academics. Because it is the easiest
technique to set up and so could be quickly and widely adopted, the fear is that
it may be put into use far too soon — outstripping our understanding of  its
safety implications and preventing any opportunity to think about how such

powerful tools should be controlled.
While ethical concerns over genetic modification are not new, particularly when
it comes to humans, they have intensified with the introduction of genome
editing for a number of reasons. First, there is no clear consensus as to whether
genome editing  is  just a further step forward, or whether  it represents a
disruptive technology capable of overcoming the current orthodoxy. If this is the
case — and  it is a very real prospect — then we will need to carefully consider
genome editing’s ethical implications and whether current regulation is adequate.
Second, there are significant ethical concerns over the potential scope and
scale of genome editing. As more researchers use CRISPR to achieve more
genome changes, the effects shift. Our consideration of a technology that is
rarely used and then only in specific cases will differ from one that is widely used
for  many   different  purposes,  because  without  oversight  and   careful
consideration, there could be all kinds of unpredictable consequences.
Genome editing techniques have so far been used to change genomes in
individual cells and in entire nonhuman organisms. Benefits have included better
targeted gene therapy  for some  diseases  in  animals.  Genetic  modification
through genome editing of plants has already created crops that are resistant
to herbicide and infection.
But more controversial is how genome editing might be used to change traits
in humans. While this has been the basis for many works of science fiction, in
real life our capacity to provide such genetic engineering has been substantially
limited.
Genome editing potentially changes  this, presenting us with the very real
possibility that any aspect of the human genome could be manipulated as we
desire. This could mean eliminating harmful genetic conditions or enhancing
traits considered advantageous. But  this  ability may also open the door to
eugenics, where those with access to the technology could select for future
generations based on traits considered merely desirable: eye, skin or hair color,
or height.
Currently, modifying plants, some animals, and non-inheritable cells in humans
is allowed under  strict controls. But  in general, modifications that  alter the
human germ-line are not allowed.
The concern instigating the US academics’ call for a moratorium is that CRISPR
Ⅶ. 심화 영어 독해Ⅰ 성취수준
could be used for altering the human germ-line: that is, making gene alterations
inheritable by our children. Gene therapies that produce non-inheritable changes
in a person's genome are ethically accepted, in part because there is no risk for
the next generation  if things go wrong.
Germ-line alterations pose much greater ethical concerns since a mistake could
harm future individuals. Of course, the flip-side is that, if carried out safely and
as  intended,  germ-line  alterations  could  also  provide  potentially permanent
solutions to genetic diseases.
There is no doubt that genome editing has enormous potential to enhance and
extend human life, and these are benefits that we can all agree on. But what is
giving so many scientists unease is the potential that genome editing could be
used in unpredictable and ultimately disastrous ways. That is why so many argue
that we ought to tread lightly and err on the side of caution, especially when it
comes to altering the very fabric of what makes us human.

2. 평가 도구
논술형
다음 법언어학(Forensic Linguistics)과 Derek Bentley 사건에 관한 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
Forensic Linguistics and the Case of Derek Bentley
There are cases where linguistic clues have helped solve actual crimes. The story
of Derek Bentley is a powerful example. Bentley was not a typical teenager — he had
an IQ of just 77 and was unable to even write his own name. On November 2, 1952,
he and his 16-year-old friend, Christopher Craig, attempted to rob a warehouse in
Croydon, South London. A young girl saw them, and her mother alerted the police.
When the officers arrived, Craig shot and killed one of them. Although Craig pulled
the trigger, Bentley was arrested, charged, and ultimately convicted of murder. On
January 28, 1953, at the age of 19, Bentley was hanged.
Bentley did not fire the gun, but he was accused of encouraging Craig by allegedly
shouting, “Let him have  it.” Both boys denied that Bentley had said anything to
provoke the shooting. However, the police submitted Bentley’s confession as evidence,
claiming  it was a verbatim record of his words, offered voluntarily and without
prompting. The jury reached a guilty verdict in less than two hours.
Bentley’s family never accepted this outcome. For decades, they fought to clear his
name. Finally, in 1998, the case reached the Court of Appeal, where a forensic linguist,
Professor Malcolm Coulthard, played a crucial role. Coulthard analyzed the confession
and demonstrated that it could not have been Bentley’s spontaneous speech. Instead,
the language revealed signs of police influence — evidence that Bentley had been
guided or questioned during the confession process.
One key clue was Bentley’s use of denials that didn’t fit the context of the narrative.
In natural  storytelling, people describe what did happen — not what  didn’t. For
example, someone is unlikely to say, “I didn’t see a dog,” unless asked, “Did you see
a dog?” In Bentley’s statement, he said, “Up to then Chris hadn’t said anything.”  Yet
at no point in the narrative had Bentley mentioned that Chris had spoken. This remark
suggested he was responding to questions — questions that were not recorded, but
likely asked during interrogation.
Another revealing feature was Bentley’s use of the word then. In everyday speech,
most people use the word order “Then I...” rather than “I then...”. However, in Bentley’s

confession, then appeared far more often than normal and frequently in the police-like
form “I then...”. Research showed that this word order was common in official police
statements but extremely rare in ordinary speech — especially from someone with
Bentley’s limited language abilities.
These patterns led Professor Coulthard to conclude that Bentley’s confession was
not a freely given, personal account of events. Rather,  it was a stitched-together
collection of responses to police prompts, edited to resemble a coherent narrative.
The  so-called  “verbatim”  statement  was,  in  reality,  heavily  influenced by  the
interrogators.
Thanks to Coulthard’s forensic linguistic analysis, the Court of Appeal overturned
Bentley’s conviction. His family finally received the justice they had pursued for nearly
50 years. Sadly, that justice came far too late — for Bentley had already paid the
ultimate price.

The sentence  “I didn’t know he was going to use the gun” appears unnecessary
in the flow of Bentley’s confession. Earlier in his narrative, Bentley had never said
anything that suggested he did know Craig would use the gun. There was also no
part of the confession that said someone had accused him of knowing  it. So this
sentence sounds like a reply to a question such as, “Did you know he was going
to shoot?” A sentence like this doesn’t usually appear in a story someone tells freely.
It suggests that Bentley was not speaking on his own, but answering questions from
the police. Since the confession was a major part of the case against him, this
undermines its credibility and supports the view that Bentley’s conviction was unjust.

by H.H. Munro
"My aunt will be down presently, Mr. Nuttel," said a very self-possessed young lady
of fifteen; "in the meantime you must try and put up with me." (1)
Framton Nuttel endeavoured to say the correct something which should duly flatter
the niece of the moment without unduly discounting the aunt that was to come.
Privately he doubted more than ever whether these formal visits on a succession of

total strangers would do much towards helping the nerve cure which he was supposed

"I know how it will be," his sister had said when he was preparing to migrate to
this rural retreat; "you will bury yourself down there and not speak to a living soul,
and your nerves will be worse than ever from moping.  I shall just give you letters of
introduction to all the people I know there. Some of them, as far as I can remember,
were quite nice." (3)
Framton wondered whether Mrs. Sappleton, the lady to whom he was presenting
one of the letters of introduction, came into the nice division. (4)
"Do you know many of the people round here?" asked the niece, when she judged
that they had had sufficient silent communion. (5)
"Hardly a soul," said Framton. "My sister was staying here, at the rectory, you know,
some four years ago, and she gave me letters of introduction to some of the people
here." (6)
He made the last statement in a tone of distinct regret. (7)
"Then you know practically nothing about my aunt?" pursued the self-possessed
young lady. (8)
"Only her name and address," admitted the caller. He was wondering whether Mrs.
Sappleton was in the married or widowed state. An undefinable something about the
room seemed to suggest masculine habitation. (9)
"Her great tragedy happened just three years ago," said the child; "that would be
since your sister's time." (10)
"Her tragedy?" asked Framton; somehow in this restful country spot tragedies
seemed out of place. (11)
"You may wonder why we keep that window wide open on an October afternoon,"
said the niece, indicating a large French window that opened on to a lawn. (12)
"It is quite warm for the time of the year," said Framton; "but has that window got
anything to do with the tragedy?" (13)
"Out through that window, three years ago to a day, her husband and her two young
brothers went off for their day's shooting. They never came back. In crossing the moor
to their favourite snipe-shooting ground they were all three engulfed in a treacherous
piece of bog... That was the dreadful part of  it." Here the child's voice lost  its
self-possessed note and became falteringly human... "Do you know, sometimes on still,
quiet evenings like this,  I almost get a creepy feeling that they will all walk in..." (14)
She broke off with a little shudder. It was a relief to Framton when the aunt bustled
into the room with a whirl of apologies for being late in making her appearance. (15)
"I hope Vera has been amusing you?" she said. (16)
"She has been very interesting," said Framton. (17)
"I hope you don't mind the open window," said Mrs. Sappleton briskly; "my husband
and brothers will be home directly from shooting, and they always come in this way..."

She rattled on cheerfully about the shooting and the scarcity of birds, and the
prospects for duck in the winter... It was certainly an unfortunate coincidence that
he should have paid his visit on this tragic anniversary. (19)
"The doctors agree in ordering me complete rest, an absence of mental excitement,
and avoidance of anything in the nature of violent physical exercise," announced
Framton... "On the matter of diet they are not so much in agreement," he continued.
"No?" said Mrs. Sappleton, in a voice which only replaced a yawn at the last moment...
"Here they are at last!" she cried. "Just in time for tea, and don't they look as if
they were muddy up to the eyes!" (22)
Framton shivered slightly and turned towards the niece... In a chill shock of nameless
fear Framton swung round in his seat and looked in the same direction. (23)
In the deepening twilight three figures were walking across the lawn towards the
window,  they all carried guns under their arms, and one of them was additionally
burdened with a white coat hung over his shoulders. A tired brown spaniel kept close
at their heels. Noiselessly they neared the house, and then a young voice chanted
out of the dusk:  "I said, Bertie, why do you bound?"(24)
Framton grabbed wildly at his stick and hat... A cyclist coming along the road had
to run into the hedge to avoid imminent collision. (25)
"Here we are, my dear," said the bearer of the white mackintosh... "Who was that
who bolted out as we came up?" (26)
"A most extraordinary man, a Mr. Nuttel," said Mrs. Sappleton... "One would think
he had seen a ghost." (27)
"I expect it was the spaniel," said the niece calmly... Enough to make anyone lose
their nerve." (28)
Romance at short notice was her speciality. (29)

2. Your Group’s First–person Narrative
It was a calm October afternoon, the kind that makes everything feel slow and quiet.
I sat in the drawing room, pretending to reread a book. The window was open, as usual.
The air was warm, but  I had something cooler in mind.
Mr. Nuttel arrived, just as my aunt had expected. He looked uncomfortable even
before he said a word. His shoulders shook a bit, and he kept glancing around like
the room might collapse.  I smiled.
"My aunt will be down presently," I said sweetly. "In the meantime, you must try and
put up with me."
He nodded, stiffly, and  I could already tell he was the perfect subject.  I asked him
a few questions, enough to confirm he didn’t know a thing about us. That’s when  I
began.
I told him the story of the tragedy: the swamp and the missing men. My voice
dropped slightly as  I spoke, and  I stared out the window, my fingers curling slowly
around the arm of the chair.
"They never came back,"  I said, softer now. "Poor Aunt Sappleton keeps the window
open every evening..."
He said nothing, but  I could feel his attention sharpen.  I added a few more details
— the waterproof coat, the song Ronnie used to sing.  I let my voice falter at just the
right moment.
Then my aunt came in, cheerful and normal. Too normal. Mr. Nuttel looked pale.
When the three of them actually appeared—guns under their arms, spaniel trotting
behind — I didn’t need to say a word. He bolted.
A pause. Then  I said, “I expect it was the spaniel. He told me he was once chased
into a grave by wild dogs.”
Romance at short notice? Oh yes. It’s always been my speciality. (289단어)

Ⅰ-5           1점  인물 대표 문장의 의미나 교차 독서의 평가가 일부 미흡함.        제공
채점 시 고려 사항
∙ Step 1에서는 제시된 문학 작품을 바탕으로 주요 등장인물 3명의 성격, 말, 행동을 원작에 충실하
게 분석하고, 모둠에서 선정한 인물이 이야기 흐름 속에서 어떤 역할을 수행하는지를 이해했는지를
평가한다. 이때 선정 이유의 타당성, 본문 근거의 명확성이 주요 평가 기준이 된다. 또한 보다 창의
적인 글쓰기를 평가하고자 할 경우에는 원작에서 거의 드러나지 않은 그 외 등장인물(Framton’s
sister, the husband, the two young brothers, and the dog)을 선정하고 원작의 흐름에 맞도
록 상상하여 쓰도록 지도할 수 있다.
∙ Step 2에서는 작품 속에서 해당 인물의 말과 행동을 명확하게 근거로 찾아내었는지를 확인한다.
확인한 근거를 바탕으로 인물 간의 상호작용 관계를 구체적으로 설명하고, 중심 인물과 주변 인물의
상호작용을 정확하게 표현했는지를 평가한다.
∙ Step 3에서는 선정한 인물의 시점으로 서사를 구성하는 활동으로, 인물의 시점에 맞게 원작의
감정·행동·상황을 적절한 언어 사용을 통해 서술하였는지를 평가한다.
∙ Step 4에서는 다른 모둠의 글을 읽고 비판적으로 감상하고 피드백을 제공하는지를 평가한다. 모둠
에서 선택한 문장의 의미 파악, 관점 전환의 효과 이해, 원작과의 비교 감상 등 해석과 성찰이
잘 드러났는지 확인하며, 이 과정에서 글쓰기 성찰 능력과 평가 참여 태도도 함께 확인한다.
∙ 채점 기준표의 채점 요소별 1점의 수행 특성보다 부족한 수행 특성을 보이는 경우는 0점으로 처리한다.

What Makes Immortal Jellyfish Immortal?
A team of researchers from the University of Oviedo in Spain mapped the genetic
sequence of the jellyfish, revealing “key molecular mechanisms behind the rejuvenation
of Turritopsis dohrnii.”
At first, gathering enough Turritopsisdohrnii to study was difficult. When it comes
to living in a tank, “they are very picky,” said Maria Pascual Torner. “And they are
very, very small, which also makes them difficult to identify and sample in the field.”
To get enough specimens, they drove a specially equipped camper van to a coast
in Italy and went diving to gather wild jellyfish. They then rushed them back to the
lab.
To trigger rejuvenation, the researchers put the jellyfish under stress by letting
them go hungry. As the medusae got smaller, changed into little balls called bud
polyps, and began remaking their adult bodies, the scientists took pictures of what
genes they were using in each phase of their development. They took some jellyfish
in each phase, froze them, and crushed them into a thick mixture to extract their
mRNA, creating a record of which genes were actively being used to make proteins.
They also compared Turritopsisdohrnii to Turritopsisrubra, a related jellyfish species
that ages normally. Researchers found that, compared to its relative, the “immortal
jellyfish” has double the amount of genes that repair and protect DNA. This allows
Turritopsis dohrnii to produce more restorative proteins.
The authors found differences in several other genes, including those associated
with reproduction and stem cell population. Normally, during the process of DNA
copying and cell division, the protective end-caps on chromosomes, called telomeres,
slowly get shorter and shorter, and when they are too short, a cell enters senescence
and can no longer keep dividing. However, “immortal jellyfish” had mutations that

preserved and maintained the telomeres. These differences may be key to the
jellyfish’s immortality.
“The most interesting thing is that it’s not a single molecular pathway... It is a
combination of many of them,” said Jan Karlseder, a molecular biologist and director
of the Glenn Center for Biology of Aging Research at the Salk Institute. “If we want
to look for an extension of a healthy lifespan, we cannot just focus on one pathway.
That will not be sufficient. We need to look at many of them and how they work
together.”
Of course, Turritopsis dohrnii is not really immortal in the manner that Qin Shi
Huang aspired to be; it can easily be killed by predators or die of disease. However,
its ability to reverse the aging process by reprogramming its cells could help develop
treatments for some of humanity’s most widespread diseases. And that would grant
an undying legacy on this tiny sea creature.

should deal with ethical dilemmas. Based on the ideas in the article, complete

Nurses’ Right
Nurses face ethical dilemmas on a daily basis regardless of where they practice.
There is no ‘right’ solution to an ethical dilemma. Ethics involve doing good and causing
no harm. But how one defines what is ethical varies from nurse to nurse and depends
on their individual values, beliefs and experiences.
There are many ethical issues nurses can experience. Patients’ quantity versus quality
in life is one of them. Quantity may address how long a person lives or perhaps how
many people will be affected by the decision. Quality relates to how good a life a
person may have, and the answer varies depending on how a person defines good.
When a patient may live longer, but will likely experience significant side effects from
the therapy, what should the nurse’s position be?
Another issue is the dilemma between patients’ freedom and the control of the
freedom. Does a patient have the right to make choices for one’s self that may result
in harm, or should the nurse prevent this choice? For example, a patient wants to
stop eating, but the nurse knows the consequences will harm the patient. In this
situation, does the nurse have the ‘right’ to force the patient to eat despite the patient’s
freedom to stop eating? Or do they have to value the patient’s choice because the
decision is about his or her body after all?
Whether nurses have to tell the truth or intentionally give incorrect information
to patients and their families is a well-known ethical issue faced by medical staff.
It becomes clear especially when families want to disagree over telling the patient
the truth about the medical condition. What should a nurse do when a family insists
that telling the patient the result will cause harm? How can a nurse know if this
is true? Does the patient have the right to know?
Ethical dilemmas in nursing come daily in which they must make a decision. A possible
procedure to deal with them may be obtaining a second opinion from other nurses
or doctors.

논술형
Read the article “How Cold Is Absolute Zero?” and complete the following
two-step task. [18점]
How Cold Is Absolute Zero?
In principle, there is no upper limit to temperature. As thermal motion increases,
a solid object first melts and then vaporizes. As the temperature is further increased,
molecules dissociate into atoms, and atoms lose some or  all of their electrons,
thereby forming a cloud of electrically charged particles—a plasma. Plasmas exist
in stars, where the temperature is many millions of degrees Celsius. Temperature
has no upper limit. In contrast, there is a definite limit at the opposite end of the
temperature scale. Gases expand when heated, and they contract when cooled.
Nineteenth century experimenters found that all gases, regardless of their initial
pressures or volumes, change by 1/273 of their volume at 0℃ for each drop in
temperature of 1 degree Celsius, provided that the pressure is held constant. So,
if a gas at 0℃ were cooled down by 273℃, it would contract 273/273 volumes and
be reduced to zero volume. Clearly, we cannot have a substance with zero volume.
The same is true of pressure. The pressure of a gas of fixed volume decreases
by 1/273 for each drop in temperature of 1 degree Celsius. If it were cooled to
273℃ below zero, it would have no pressure at all. In practice, every gas converts
to a liquid before becoming this cold. Nevertheless, these decreases by 1/273
increments suggested the idea of the lowest temperature: -273℃. That’s the lower
limit of temperature, absolute zero. At this temperature, molecules have lost all
available kinetic energy. No more energy can be removed from a substance at
absolute zero.  It can’t get any colder.
The absolute temperature scale is called the Kelvin scale, named after the famous
British mathematician and physicist William Thomson, First Baron Kelvin. Absolute
zero is 0 K (short for “zero kelvin”); note that the word ‘degrees’ is not used with
Kelvin temperatures. There are no negative numbers on the Kelvin scale.  Its
temperature divisions are identical to the divisions on the Celsius scale. Thus, the
melting point of ice is 273K, and the boiling point of water is 373K.

of absolute zero. First, the writer uses cause and effect to explain what happens as

behavior of gases. Second, the  writer uses numerical examples to support the
explanation. The text states that gas volume and pressure decrease by 1/273 for every
one-degree drop in temperature, leading to the conclusion that –273°C marks the
theoretical point of zero volume and pressure. This use of exact numbers gives the
explanation scientific credibility and makes the concept easier to grasp. Finally, the
writer introduces the Kelvin scale and compares  it with the Celsius  scale. This
comparison helps place absolute zero in a familiar context. Overall, by combining logical
strategies like cause and effect, numerical reasoning, and comparison, the writer makes
a complex scientific idea more understandable and convincing for general readers.

Dear Mr. Waters,
I am in receipt of your electronic mail dated the 14th of April and duly
impressed by the Shakespearean complexity of your tragedy. ⓐ Everyone in
this tale has a rock-solid hamartia: hers, that she is so sick; yours, that you
are so well. Were she better or you sicker, then the stars would not be so
terribly  crossed, but  it  is the nature of  stars to  cross, and never was
Shakespeare more wrong than when he had Cassius note, ⓑ “The fault, dear
Brutus, is not in our stars / But in ourselves.” Easy enough to say when you’re
a Roman nobleman (or Shakespeare!), but there is no shortage of fault to be
found amid our stars.
While we’re on the topic of old Will’s insufficiencies, your writing about
young Hazel reminds me of the Bard’s Fifty-fifth sonnet, which of course
begins, “Not marble, nor the gilded monuments / Of princes, shall outlive this
powerful rhyme; / But you shall shine more bright in these contents / Than
unswept stone, besmear’d with sluttish time.” (Off topic, but: What a slut time
is. She screws everybody.) It’s a fine poem but a deceitful one: We do indeed
remember Shakespeare’s powerful rhyme, but what do we remember about
the person  it commemorates? Nothing. We’re pretty sure he was male;
everything else is guesswork. Shakespeare told us precious little of the man
whom he entombed in his linguistic sarcophagus. (Witness also that when we
talk about literature, we do so in the present tense. When we speak of the
dead, we are not so kind.) You do not immortalize the lost by writing
about them. Language buries, but does not resurrect. (Full disclosure:  I am
not the first to make this observation. cf, the MacLeish poem “Not Marble, Nor
the Gilded Monuments,” which contains the heroic line “I shall say you will die
and none will remember you.”)

It means that each main character has a decisive tragic flaw—Hazel’s is her severe
illness and Augustus’s is his being comparatively well—and this contrast makes their
“stars” cross, framing the tragedy as fate rather than personal blame.
[Step 2]
The Fault in Our Stars refers to the idea that some problems in life are beyond
human control. In the novel, Hazel and Augustus both suffer from cancer, which was
not caused by any fault of their own. This contrasts with Shakespeare’s original line,
which claims that we are responsible for our fate. Hazel and Augustus, however, see
their suffering as written in the stars—a matter of fate, not choice. Augustus tries to
make meaning out of his life despite his illness, while Hazel tries to protect those she
loves from the pain of her disease. The title reflects their belief that not all tragedies
are the result of personal flaws, but rather the result of uncontrollable circumstances.

[Step 1] Text Reading: What Are Microaggressions?
What Are Microaggressions?
The term “microaggression” originated from Harvard University professor Chester
Middlebrook Pierce in his work with Black Americans. He defined microaggressions
as  subtle,  stunning,  often  automatic,  and  nonverbal  exchanges  that  are
“put-downs.” Microaggressions have the potential to impact any oppressed group
psychologically and can be linked to racism, genderism, and other forms of
oppression.
Racial microaggressions, such as assumptions about a person’s intelligence or
work ethic based on their race or ethnicity, are commonplace verbal, nonverbal, or
environmental indignities, whether intentional or unintentional, that communicate
hostile or negative racial insults. Similarly, unfair and unequal treatment of women
can manifest in discriminatory hiring or hostile work environments. Moreover,
experiential microaggressions are also common and can be seen in statements that
dismiss an individual’s cultural background or experiences. These microaggressions
make target groups feel unwelcome, isolated, and unsafe.
A  specific instance  involving a man with  visual impairment  highlights how
microaggressions affect individuals with disabilities. When people speak to him,
they often raise their voices. A well-meaning nurse was actually “yelling at him”
when giving him directions on taking his medication. He replied to her: “Please
don’t raise your voice,  I can hear you perfectly well.” People raising their voices
while speaking to him implied a hidden message that a person with a disability is
defined as lesser in all aspects of functioning.
Countless examples of microaggression are delivered daily without perpetrators’
awareness. Although these actions may appear harmless or innocent in nature,
they  are  nevertheless damaging  to  targets because they  result  in harmful
psychological consequences and create inequalities. It cannot be overstated how
crucial it is to recognize the impact of microaggressions and work towards their
elimination in order to create a more equitable future where everyone is treated
with respect and dignity.

is the victim, never gets to tell its side of the story—so the real truth can never
be known, only the hunter’s version of the truth.
Fresh out of my doctoral program,  I met a Nigerian scholar who was amused
by my commitment  to  seeking knowledge through  experimentation and
experience. He shared with me a tale often told to children in his country about
a female elementary school teacher who posed a math problem to her class:
“Suppose there are four blackbirds sitting on a tree branch. You take a slingshot
and shoot one of them. How many are left?”
A White student answered quickly, “That’s easy, Teacher. Four take away one
is three.” An equally eager Nigerian immigrant boy stated with equal certainty
that the answer was zero. The teacher chuckled at the Nigerian youth, indicated
the answer was wrong, and suggested he study more math. From that day on,
the young boy seemed to withdraw from class activities and seldom spoke to
his classmates or teacher.
If the teacher had pursued the reasons behind the Nigerian student’s answer,
she might have heard the following: “If you shoot one bird, the others will fly
away.” Herein lies a major worldview difference between that of the teacher
and the African youth. From a Western science perspective, the math problem
represents a hypothetical situation that requires a literal, task-based answer.
From the perspective of the Nigerian student, however, his answer is based
on lived experience, a known relationship with birds, and an understanding of

how the real—that is, not hypothetical—world operates.
Seen from the perspective of the hunter and the lion, both answers may be
considered correct, but, unfortunately, it is the hunter’s tale that determines
“truth” and can result in cultural oppression, imposing one reality over another,
with devastating consequences. As for the Nigerian boy, he  is  left feeling
dismissed, inadequate, and isolated from the curriculum and teacher. His school
performance  is  likely to  suffer. This  is the  invisible world of  experiential
microaggressions, unseen by the hunter.

Article Style
Title: The Hidden Harm of Everyday Words: Understanding Microaggressions
Have you ever said something you thought was harmless, only to find out it hurt
Ⅷ. 심화 영어 독해Ⅱ 성취수준
someone deeply? These subtle actions or comments are known as microaggressions.
They are small, often unintentional, but they send negative messages to marginalized
groups.
For example, imagine a student from another country being told, “Wow, your English
is so good!” Although the speaker may intend to compliment, the hidden message is
that the student is an outsider who doesn’t belong.
These everyday comments may seem insignificant, but they can lead to feelings of
isolation, stress, and low self-esteem. Over time, they create barriers and reinforce
inequality.
We can  all make a difference. Think before you speak. Ask yourself: Could this
comment carry an unintended message? By becoming aware and changing small
behaviors, we can create a more respectful and inclusive world.
Lecture Style(Speech)
Hello everyone, my name  is [Student Name], and today   I want to  talk about
something we often overlook—microaggressions.
First, let me ask you this: Have you ever been asked, “Where are you really from?”
At first, it might sound like an innocent question. But to the person being asked, it
may suggest: “You don’t belong here.” Microaggressions are subtle words or actions
that send  hurtful messages to people from marginalized groups. They may be
unintentional, but they have real consequences. They can make someone feel invisible,
unworthy, or unwelcome.
Let me share a quick example. A visually impaired man was often shouted at by
people trying to help him. They thought they were being kind, but their raised voices
implied he was less capable in all aspects. Imagine how that must have felt.
So, what can we do? We need to listen, reflect, and choose our words carefully. Most
importantly, we must  learn  from  the  perspectives  of  those who  experience
microaggressions. Small changes in our language can lead to big changes in someone’s
life. Thank you.

Many students identify consciously or unconsciously as nomophobes when  it
comes to using cell phones. ‘Nomophobia’ is the fear of being away from a
mobile phone. The term ‘nomophobia’ is an abbreviation for ‘no-mobile-phone
phobia.’ A feeling of anxiety washes over people suffering from nomophobia
when they lose contact with their phones. Signs of nomophobia are easy to
notice. Never turning  off the phone, taking the phones everywhere, and
obsessively checking missed texts and calls are clear signs. Using phones at
inappropriate times and missing opportunities for face-to-face interaction and
preferring over the phone contact are indicators as well. Physical side effects
can occur for nomophobes when their phone dies or is otherwise unusable.
These symptoms include panic attacks, shortness of breath, sweating, increased
heart rate, or chest pain. Millions of people suffer from nomophobia around the
globe. The most common sufferers are in the 18–21 age range, making high
school students likely candidates.

Hearing is simply the process of perceiving sounds within our environment. The
best way to illustrate hearing is through the biological processes involved in sensory
perception. Listening, on the other hand, goes beyond simply picking up stimuli
around us and identifying what these stimuli are. Listening involves the extra steps
of really understanding what we heard and giving  it deliberate attention and
thoughtful  consideration.  It may be  said  that  listening  involves more  active
participation from a person than simply hearing. During communication, taking the
extra step to move from hearing to listening can enhance a person’s interpersonal
relationships  in many ways. Listening promotes a more accurate and deeper
understanding of a person’s communication, helping a responder to provide the
most appropriate response. But more so, when you’re listening to a person, you
communicate to them that you value not just what they are saying, but their
presence as well.
<출처: NE능률(허명혜 외, 2015), 심화 영어 작문I, p.35>

among other voices and background noise.

Putting Korea’s Heart in a Bowl: Making Kimchi
Have you ever tried food that’s spicy, sour, and full of tradition all at the same time?
Then you must try kimchi, Korea’s most famous fermented dish made with cabbage,
radish, and chili pepper. One of the best places to experience it is the Kimchi Museum
in Seoul, where you can learn its history and even make your own kimchi! Kimchi is
more than just a side dish—it’s a symbol of Korean culture. While it can be compared
to sauerkraut in Germany or pickles in the U.S., kimchi has a unique taste and is deeply
connected to Korean family  life and seasonal traditions  like Kimjang, the winter
kimchi-making season. To enjoy it fully, try making kimchi yourself in a hands-on class.
It’s a fun way to understand Korean flavors and values. If you like trying new foods
and cultures, kimchi is a delicious place to start.

You may have noticed that more and more people in Korea are raising cats and
dogs these days. This is happening especially as our society ages and more families
consist of just two generations. While the pet industry is growing quickly, there's

are already homeless. And to keep public places clean and safe, we should allow
pets in those areas—but with clear rules and restrictions.

※ Trolley Dilemma에 관한 다음 글을 읽고, 주어진 질문에 답하시오. [8점]
An ethical dilemma is a situation where  it is difficult to say what is right or
wrong. The Trolley Problem is a well-known example. A trolley is running out of
control, and if it stays on its current track, it will hit five people. You have the
option to flip a switch and send the trolley onto another track, where only one
person is tied. In this case, doing nothing means five people will die, while taking
action  will cause one person’s death. This situation creates a  difficult moral
question: Should we act to save more lives, or avoid being responsible for killing
someone? Some people follow Utilitarianism, which says the best action is the one
that benefits the most people. From this view, flipping the switch is the right
choice. Others believe it is wrong to take an action that directly causes someone’s
death, even  if more people are saved. These different opinions show that even
simple decisions can involve complex moral values.

글쓰기와 시각 자료 제작이 결합된 과제의 특성을 반영하여, 학생이 계획적으로 정보를
활용 시
정리하고, 대상과 목적에 적합한 실용문을 구성할 수 있도록 단계별로 지원하였다.
고려 사항
사전 활동을 통해 생태관광과 관련된 어휘, 표현, 구조적 틀을 연습함으로써, 본문 작성 및
PPT 구성에 대한 인지적 부담을 줄이고 작문 활동의 몰입도를 높였다.
성취기준 [12심작Ⅱ04-01], [12심작Ⅱ04-04], [12심작Ⅱ04-08]에 근거하여, 학생이 홍보
목적에 맞는 서식을 작성하고, 우리 문화를 조리 있게 소개하며, 주어진 주제에 대한 자기
생각을 설득력 있게 표현하는 능력을 종합적으로 평가할 수 있도록 하였다.

▣ Ecotourism에 관한 다음 글을 읽고, 물음에 답하시오.
Ecotourism means  all  nature-based forms  of  tourism  in which  the main
motivation of the tourists is the observation and appreciation of nature as well as
the traditional cultures prevailing in natural areas. They are experiences that are
managed to ensure they are ecologically, economically and socially sustainable,
contributing to the well-being of the natural areas and local communities where
they  operate.   It  contains  educational  features  for  those  interested   in
understanding and preserving the nature and  local  culture. To minimize the
damage massive commercial tourism may cause,  it  is exclusively organized by
specialized tour operators for small groups. Service provider partners at the
destinations  tend  to  be  small,  locally owned  businesses.  Consequently,   it
generates  economic  benefits  for  the  host  communities,  organizations  and
authorities managing natural areas with conservation purposes, promoting the
awareness towards the conservation of natural and cultural assets, both among
locals and tourists.

[평가문항_소개 글]
Jeju Gotjawal Forest is a unique and beautiful place located on Jeju Island, South
Korea. What makes it special is that it sits on ancient lava rocks, creating a unique
Ⅹ. 심화 영어 작문Ⅱ 성취수준
ecosystem. The forest is filled with green trees, mossy stones, and quiet trails. Even
in summer, it stays cool and peaceful, making it a perfect place to escape the heat
and enjoy nature.
You can get to Gotjawal Forest by taking a bus or taxi from Jeju Airport. It takes
about 40 minutes. Visitors can walk along eco-trails, breathe in clean, fresh air, and
listen to the sounds of birds. Local people run eco-programs through which tourists
can learn about native plants, plant trees, or help clean the forest. There are also local
products like Jeju honey and herbal tea sold by the community to support the local
economy.
I recommend Gotjawal because it is rewarding and relaxing. It is not crowded like
other tourist spots, so people can enjoy its peace and quiet. The forest shows how
tourism can help protect nature and support local communities.  If you care about
protecting the Earth and want to experience something special, come and explore
Gotjawal Forest.

  1   주요 용어 설명


 성취기준: 학생들이 각 교과(목)의 “영역별 내용 요소(지식･이해, 과정･기능, 가치･

   태도)1)를 학습한 결과, 궁극적으로 할 수 있거나 할 수 있기를 기대하는 도달점”을

  진술한 것.

 성취수준: 학생들이 각 교과목 성취기준(들)에 도달한 정도를 나타낸 것. 즉, 학생들

  의 도달 정도를 몇 개의 수준으로 구분하고, 각 수준에 속한 학생들이 무엇을

  알고 할 수 있는지를 기술한 것. 성취기준별 성취수준과 영역별 성취수준 등이

   있음.

  - 성취기준별 성취수준: 성취기준 단위 성취수준으로, 학교급･교과목･성취기준의

   특성에 따라 3수준 또는 5수준으로 구분하여 진술한 것.

  - 성취기준별 성취수준은 학교 특성에 따라 현장에서 변형하여 활용하기보다는,

   본 현장보급본을 통해 개발･보급한 것을 그대로 활용할 것을 권고함.

  - 영역별 성취수준: 영역 단위 성취수준으로, 영역 내 성취기준들을 포괄하는 전반적

   인 특성을 학교급･교과목의 특성에 따라 3수준 또는 5수준으로 구분하여 진술한

    것. 단, 외국어ㆍ국제 계열 고등학교 선택과목의 경우, 내용 영역 구분이 없는

   과목이 많아 ‘영역별 성취수준’을 개발하지 않았음2).

  기능하는 일체를 통칭함.

 1) 2022 개정 교과 교육과정 내용 체계 및 성취기준의 구성 범주를 의미한다. 본 연구에서 개발 준거로 삼은 성취기준이
   2015 개정 교과 교육과정에 해당하는 교과의 경우에는 명시적으로 3가지 구성 범주를 취하고 있지는 않다. 이에,
   2015 개정 교육과정과 2022 개정 교육과정 취지를 종합적으로 고려하여 성취기준별 성취수준을 개발하였다.
 2) 영역별 성취수준 개발 절차 및 방법에 관해서는 Ⅱ장 2절을 참고.

Ⅰ. 성취수준 개발의 이해


  3   성취기준별 성취수준 개발


가. 개발 개요

교과 교육과정의 내용 체계와 성취기준(들)을 분석하여 지식･이해, 과정･기능,

  가치･태도의 위계나 수준을 고려하여 성취기준별로 성취수준 작성.

3수준 체계(A, B, C) 또는 5수준 체계(A, B, C, D, E)로 개발하되, 성취기준 내용

  요소의 복합성 정도에 따라 수준 구별.



 ￭ 성취수준 구분의 원리
   - 지식의 개념 위계나 이해의 깊이를 활용하여 수준을 구분한다.
   - 과정･기능 수행 정도나 맥락과 상황 변인으로 차별화하여 수준을 구분한다.
   - 가치･태도의 내면화와 실천과 참여 등으로 수준을 구분한다.

① 영역의 내용 체계와 성취기준(들)의 지식･이해, 과정･기능, 가치･태도의 내용 요소

  추출 및 위계 분석

② 영역 내 성취기준이 포함하고 있는 지식･이해, 과정･기능, 가치･태도의 내용 요소

  수준 및 위계 분석

  - 교과(과목)의 영역 특성에 따라 내용 체계에 제시된 ‘가치･태도’ 범주의 내용

   요소가 성취기준에서 명시적으로 드러나지 않더라도, 교육과정 취지를 살려 영역

   내 성취수준들에서 ‘가치･태도’ 범주 관련 내용을 되도록 반영함.

③ 영역 내 성취기준이 포함하고 있는 내용 요소들의 복합성 등을 고려하여 3수준

  또는 5수준의 진술문 개발

  - 지식･이해, 과정･기능, 가치･태도의 각 범주는 그 특성을 고려하여 수준을 구분하고

   이를 복합적으로 구성하여 수준을 진술함.

④ 성취기준별 성취수준 작성 후 각 영역 간 수준 진술 정도, 전후 학년(군)과의 능력

  진술 위계 등을 점검

  - 같은 학년(군)에서 영역 내는 물론 영역 간 성취수준의 진술 정도를 각 수준별로

   점검하여 작성함.

  - 학년(군)이 높아짐에 따라 성취수준 간의 위계가 나타나는지 점검함. 다만, 교과

   및 범주 특성에 따라 학년(군)이 높아져도 동일 수준 진술이 반복적으로 나타날

   수 있음.

  1   성취기준 도달 정도 예측 및 개념화 근거



 성취기준은 수업 및 평가의 근거로서의 역할을 하지만 성취기준 자체는 도달

  정도에 대한 정보가 부족하여 추가적으로 성취수준에 대한 정보가 필요하다. 교사

  는 성취수준에 대한 일관된 이해를 가지고 수업과 평가를 계획하고 운영해야

  하는데 성취기준별 성취수준이나 영역별 성취수준은 이러한 이해와 개념화에

  도움을 줄 수 있다.

 성취기준별 성취수준은 각 성취기준에 도달한 정도를 해당 교과목 평정 단계에

  따라 구체화하여 제시한 것으로 성취기준별로 도달할 수행 목표를 예측하거나

  가늠할 수 있다. 영역별 성취수준은 해당 교과목의 영역별로 도달할 목표를 범주

   (지식･이해, 과정･기능, 가치･태도)에 따라 제시한 것으로 교과목 전체 수준에서

  각 범주별로 도달할 수행 목표를 예측하거나 가늠할 수 있다.



  • 성취기준별 성취수준은 각 성취기준에 도달한 정도를 해당 교과목 평정 단계에 따라 구체화하여
  제시한 것으로 성취기준별로 도달할 수행 목표를 예측하거나 가늠할 수 있음.
  • 영역별 성취수준은 해당 교과목의 영역별로 도달할 목표를 범주(지식･이해, 과정･기능, 가치･태도)에
  따라 제시한 것으로 교과목 전체 수준에서 각 범주별로 도달할 수행 목표를 예측하거나 가늠할
  수 있음.



 이러한 성취수준은 수업 설계와 평가 문항 제작에서 도달 정보나 목표를 개념화할

  때도 근거가 된다. 교사 간 유사한 수준에 대한 개념을 가질 수 있도록 도움을

   준다. 이때 수준 구분에 대한 유연성은 열어두되, 수준에 대한 교사 간 해석의

  폭을 최대한 좁혀 교육과정 범위 내에서 수업과 평가가 실행되도록 하기 위함이다.

 첫째, 한 학기 수업을 통해 각 수준의 학생들이 도달해야 할 목표가 되므로 수업의

    준거가 된다.

 둘째, 한 학기 동안의 성취기준에 대한 도달 정도를 평가할 때 미리 설정한 학기

    단위 성취수준은 평가 활동의 준거가 된다.

 셋째, 학생들이 무엇을 알고 할 수 있는지 기술하므로 개별 학생의 평가 결과를 보고하고

   기록하는 준거가 된다.


다. 학생 수준을 고려한 수업 설계에 활용

성취기준별/영역별 성취수준은 학생 수준을 고려한 수업 설계에 활용될 수 있다.

우선, 학생 맞춤형 수업 설계에 활용될 수 있다. 2022 개정 교육과정은 학생

  개별화 맞춤형 수업을 강조하고 있다. 이러한 취지에 따라 학생 맞춤형 수업을

  설계하기 위해서 학생 수준에 맞는 진단과 학습 지원이 필요하다. 이를 위해서는

  학생 수준의 진단 도구 개발 및 진단 평가 시행이 필요하다. 이때 성취기준별/영역별

  성취수준이 활용될 수 있다.

라. 평가 도구 제작 및 채점 기준 설정의 근거로 활용


  1) 평가 도구 제작의 근거로 활용

우선, 성취기준을 분석하여 성취기준에 도달하기 위한 과정에서 필요한 능력을

  평가 요소의 형태로 구체화하고, 평가 요소를 가장 적합하게 평가할 수 있는 평가

  방법을 선정한다. 성취기준을 분석하여 평가 방법을 선정한 다음, 학기 단위로

  평가 계획서를 작성한다.

이때 ‘평가 요소’란 교육과정 성취기준 도달의 증거로 학생들이 보여주기를 기대하

  는 핵심 내용을 구체적으로 기술한 평가 내용을 의미한다. 평가 요소는 성취기준을

  분석하여 해당 성취기준에의 도달 정도를 판단하기 위해서 어떠한 내용을 평가해

  야 하는지를 기준으로 작성한다. 평가 요소는 평가의 목표와 특성을 고려하여

  교육과정 성취기준에서 도출하며, 학생들의 수행 정도를 판단할 수 있도록 지식,

   기능, 태도와 같은 구체적인 내용으로 기술한다.


  2) 채점 기준 설정의 근거로 활용

성취수준은 수행평가(또는 서･논술형 문항) 도구 제작 및 채점 기준 설정의 근거로

   활용된다.

채점 기준을 설정할 때에는 모든 성취수준(A~E)을 평가할 수 있도록 수행평가

  과제(또는 서･논술형 문항) 및 채점 기준을 개발한다. 모든 성취수준의 학생들이

  수행할 수 있는 과제로 문항을 구성할 필요가 있다.


마. 성취 결과 산출 및 보고의 근거로 활용

성취기준별/영역별 성취수준과 이를 활용하여 개발된 학기 단위 성취수준을 토대로

  학생의 성취수준을 산출한다. 분할점수 설정과 평가 시행이 완료되면 지필평가와

  수행평가 점수를 합산하여 성취율에 따라 학생의 성취도를 산출한다. 즉, 개별

  학생에 대해 A~E 또는 A~C의 성취수준을 산출한다.

이러한 성취도 산출 과정을 통한 성적 결과 보고 시, 학기 단위 성취수준과

  연계하여 학생의 실제 수행 능력을 진술한다. 각 성취수준에 해당하는 학생이

  무엇을 알고 할 수 있는지의 교수･학습 정보를 보고한다. 개별 학생이 알고 할

  수 있는 것을 기술할 때는 미리 진술한 학기 단위 성취수준을 중심으로 개별

  학생의 수행 능력을 진술한다.

이러한 정보를 학생에게 피드백한다. 피드백은 학생의 학습 상태에 대한 정보를

  제공하여 학생의 학습과 성장을 지원하는 전체적인 과정이다. 학생의 교육 목표

  도달도를 확인하고 교수･학습 개선에 활용할 수도 있다. 피드백은 점수나 성취도

  를 알려주거나 정답 여부를 알려주는 것에서부터 개별 학생의 강약점이나 추후

  학습 방향, 성장 정도 등을 알려주는 등 다양한 유형이 있다.

   Title: Talchum – Korea’s Traditional Mask Dance

  Good morning, everyone. Today, we would like to introduce Talchum, one of Korea’s most
unique  intangible  cultural  heritages. Talchum  is a  traditional mask dance that was
developed in various regions, such as Hahoe and Bongsan. In the past, it was performed
by ordinary people as social satire, criticizing injustice, while wishing for harmony and
happiness. Talchum  includes  colorful  masks,  rhythmic  music, and  dramatic dance
movements. Performers also told humorous stories during the performance. What makes
it really special is how it combines entertainment with deep cultural meaning. Even today,
Talchum is performed at festivals and by cultural organizations. Many local communities
and artists work together to preserve this cultural performance. Personally,  I find  it
fascinating because it reflects Korean history and humor in a creative and artistic way.

regions of Korea, such as Hahoe and Bongsan. It was created by ordinary people to express

their thoughts and feelings in creative ways.


Student 2 – Cultural Meaning (문화적 의미)

  Talchum is more than just a performance. It is satire. It expresses a desire for healing,

and social justice. Performers use masks and gestures to criticize unfair systems and to

hope for a better  life. This shows the spirit of Korean people—creative, strong, and

humorous.


Student 3 – Key Features (주요 특징)

  Talchum has many  special  features.  It  includes  colorful masks,  dramatic dance

movements, and  live music. The stories are often funny and  full of meaning. Each

movement and costume carries a message, and the audience can also join in the fun.

           ceremonial, Talchum is a way for common people to share their voice.

∙ [STEP 1] ‘유네스코 무형유산 개념 요약’은 정보 수용 및 재구성 능력을 평가하는 문항으로, 내용의

 정확성, 어휘(UNESCO, intangible heritage, preserve) 사용의 적절성, 그리고 사례 포함 여부와

 요약문의 명료성에 초점을 두어 평가한다.

∙ [STEP 2] ‘무형유산 조사 활동’은 조사 항목별 정보를 정확하고 충실하게 수집했는지, 그리고 발표

 준비를 위한 기초 정보를 논리적이고 간결하게 정리했는지에 중점을 두어 평가한다.

∙ [STEP 2] ‘발표 대본 작성’에서는 ① 조사 항목을 바탕으로 한 내용 완성도와 ② 공식적인 발표

 상황에 적합한 언어 사용이 모두 고려된다. 형식만 갖추고 내용이 피상적일 경우에는 감점될 수

 있으며, 단순한 정보 나열보다는 청중을 고려한 발표문 구성이 이루어졌는지 확인한다.

∙ [STEP 2] ‘시각 자료 구성’에서는 발표 내용과의 일치성, 정보의 시각적 전달 효과, 그리고 유네스코

 무형유산이라는 주제에 대한 시각적 강조 표현 여부가 주요 평가 요소이다.

∙ [STEP 3] 발표 실연은 단순히 대본을 잘 암기했는지를 평가하는 것이 아니라, 내용 전달력, 영어

 표현의 적절성, 발표자 간 협업 및 역할 수행, 그리고 질문에 대한 논리적이고 명확한 응답(Q&A)을

 통해 이루어진다. 발표 전 점검표를 바탕으로 연습하고 동료에게 피드백을 제공했는지 여부도 함께

 평가에 반영된다. 대본을 그대로 읽기만 할 경우, 대본 점수는 인정되지만 실제 발표 점수는 감점될

   Hello listeners! This is Culture Inside. Thank you for tuning in. Have you ever heard
of “personal space”? It is the invisible private area around us that we like to keep
to ourselves when we’re talking to someone. Now, here’s the interesting part—how
much space we like can really depend on who we are and where we’re from. For
example, in the U.S., people generally like to keep a little more distance. Americans
tend to value their personal space a lot, and if someone steps in too close, it can
feel uncomfortable or even a bit rude. However, in Brazil, it’s a whole different story!
People in Brazil are usually much more comfortable standing close to one another.
It’s totally normal for them to chat at a closer distance, and things like a friendly pat
on the arm or a light touch on the shoulder? No big deal—it’s part of how they
connect. So while that kind of closeness might lead to discomfort for some Americans,
for many Brazilians, it’s just a natural way to build trust and warmth in conversation.
Isn’t  it fascinating how something as simple as space can reflect so much about
culture? Stay with us—there’s more coming up on Culture Inside!

∙ [Step 1] ‘뉴스 요약’은 정보 이해 및 재구성 능력을 평가하는 문항으로, 내용 정확성, 어휘 사용의

 적절성, 요약문의 명료성에 초점을 두어 평가한다.

∙ [Step 2-3] 이 단계에서는 학생이 맡은 역할의 관점을 잘 이해하고 표현했는지가 핵심 평가 요소이

 경우 감점된다.

∙ [Step 2-4] 반론과 응답이 모두 제시되었는지 확인하며, 반론의 설득력과 응답의 논리성을 각각

다음 글의 내용을 바탕으로 질투의 두 가지 유형을 비교하고, 관용구 “keeping up with the

            Keep up with the Joneses or Forget the Joneses?

  “Keeping up with the Joneses” is a well–known English idiom, which originally came
from the famous comic strip with the same title. First created in 1913, the strip ran
until 1940 in various newspapers. The strip depicts the socially ambitious McGinis
family, who struggle to “keep up” with their neighbors, the Joneses. The secret of
the comic strip’s enduring fame lies in the fact that it deals with a well–known aspect
of the human condition: envy. But a new study finds that depending on the nature
of your envy — benign or malicious, that is — you will pay more to either imitate the
Joneses or get something different.
  Researchers  in  the  Netherlands  studied  envy–motivated  behavior  by  asking
students to imagine that a friend has a new smartphone that they desire. The
students were then asked  if they felt just positively envious of the fellow student
(benign) or envious and bitter (malicious).
  The result showed a complex pattern of decision making. Participants who felt
benign envy said they were willing to pay more to have the same smartphone that
the envied person has. But people who were maliciously envious were more likely to
pay more for a different brand of smartphone.
  Van de Ven, one of the researchers, explains that benign envy exists  if people
think the other person deserves the reward they also seek. So when you see a friend
is enjoying a new smartphone, you believe you deserve it as well and you are willing
to pay more to get the same item. Benign envy motivates you to obtain the same
reward that your friend enjoys by moving yourself up. On the other hand, malicious
envy occurs if people think the other person is inferior to them and undeserving of
the reward. Therefore, if you maliciously envy your friend’s smartphone, you are likely
to pay more for a competitive but slightly different item because you wish to prove
your superiority by degrading the other person’s new item. Malicious envy creates a
desire to pull down the other person.

              Creating an icon is not an easy task for a designer

     Because an icon must be universal, it can be very tricky for a designer to create
   a workable icon. There are so many things to take into consideration. For example,
   a representation  of something could be  interpreted  differently depending on
   someone’s culture, beliefs or religion. Colors might also need to be avoided. In
   Europe, red is a common symbol for danger, but in China, red symbolizes good
   fortune and is believed to keep away evil.
    Some words are considered impossible to translate into a pictogram without the
   help of text. Try to represent an ‘account manager’ as an icon for example. It might
   not seem too hard at first, but when you think about it, you’ll soon realize that it’s
   not an easy task at  all.
        It’s also very risky to try to do something differently when creating a new icon.
     If a triangle in a circle means play, don’t try to reinvent the wheel.  It’ll simply
   confuse people. Icons are not always the place to be creative.

            Are some of the existing icons  still up to date today?

    When you look at some of today’s most popular icons, a question may pop into
   your head: “How long are we going to keep these without updating them?” This
   question applies particularly to technology, which is constantly evolving year after
    year. Electronic devices become smaller, thinner, able to perform two or more tasks
   simultaneously and equipped with touch screens. Their shapes are also changing,
   as well as the way we are using them.

                       Is this icon  still correctly understood today?

     Generation Z was born with tablets and smart phones, so can they really identify
   the old-fashioned phone receiver we use to represent calls? Are they aware that
   the voicemail icon is actually a tape recorder? Do they actually know what a tape
   recorder is? Those are the kinds of questions to bring up when looking at smart
   phones or computers. It seems that those types of icons have become ideograms
   instead  of  pictograms, as they seem  to be symbols  that have  finally been
    universally accepted as the official representation of an idea or concept.

   A SWOT analysis is a framework and a diagnostic tool that is used to help you
  understand the external and internal factors which can influence a project or an
  organisation. The name is an acronym for the four elements of a SWOT analysis
  which are:


    1. Strengths: These are positive contributions that have happened during the
    timescale of an activity/project that should be celebrated. This would include any
    advantages to the organisation such as upskilling, reputation, resources etc...,

    2. Weaknesses: These are activities or areas that have been identified could be
    improved such as any gaps, inefficiencies etc...,

    3. Opportunities: These offer any opportunities for improvement that will contribute
    to strengthening your project or organisation that you could take advantage of,

    4. Threats: These are external factors that can negatively affect the performance
    or survival of project. External means that they are usually outside of the
    departments or organisations control.


    Strengths and Weaknesses are seen as intrinsic within a project or organisation
  whereas Opportunities and Threats are seen as extrinsic factors that occur outside
  of the organisations control. A SWOT analysis allows you to generate information
  so that you can evaluate the current situation, identifying areas to improve and
  grow and address any challenges in achieving goals that have been created for a
  project or organisation.

  appealing to younger users.

  symbol for live messaging, and the camera inside highlights how important photo

  sharing is for today’s users. Compared to an envelope, this combination offers a more

  symbolic meaning for how communication actually happens in this app. Second, the

 new color choice helps the app stand out on users’ screens. Bright purple gives a

  fun, friendly impression, which fits well with the app’s teenage audience.

    In conclusion, we believe that a meaningful and familiar icon can make a big

  difference in how users feel about an app. Our redesigned icon not only looks more

  modern, but it also represents the actual way people communicate today, through

  images, chatting, and fast interaction. That’s why this new design is a better fit for

  AAATalk and its users.

    and the profit in a restaurant. Let’s imagine Jane opened a restaurant with one
     waiter. The food was good, but customers had to wait too long to be served.
    As a result, Jane’s profits were only $4,000 per month. She decided to hire a
    second waiter, which increased her profits to $6,000. A third waiter boosted
    her profits to $6,500. However, when Jane hired a fourth waiter, her profits
    decreased to $5,500. This shows that there is an optimal number of waiters
     for a restaurant. When there are too few waiters, customers have to wait too
     long and profits suffer. However, when there are too many waiters, they can
    get in each other’s way and productivity decreases. As a result, profits start
     to decline. The optimal number of waiters for a restaurant will vary depending
    on the size of the restaurant, the type of food it serves, and the number of
    customers it typically serves. However, this concept shows that there is a point
     at which adding more waiters will no longer increase profits.

다음은 신경 가소성과 학습(neuroplasticity and learning)에 관한 글이다. 글을 읽고, 밑줄
친 the “fire together, wire together” principle이 다음 글에서 의미하는 바를 <조건>에
맞게 영어로 기술하시오. [8점]

    In the past, scientists believed that the brain ceased to develop after childhood.
 But recent studies indicate that the brain is able to continue growing and evolving
 throughout one’s life. This is called neuroplasticity, which refers to the ability of
 the brain to change and adapt in response to life experiences. Neuro refers to
 neurons, the nerve cells in the brain and nervous system. Plasticity is the capacity
 to be shaped and altered. The brain’s neuroplasticity allows it to reorganize neural
 pathways and to create new connections at any age.

    Until the age of three, a child’s brain undergoes significant change. The young
 brain experiences developmental plasticity as its neurons rapidly grow branches.
 Synapses, the places where neurons connect and communicate with one another,
 are formed at a faster rate than at any other time. At birth, the number of
 synapses  per  neuron  is  2,500,  but  by  the age two  or  three,  there  are
 approximately 15,000 synapses per neuron. This amount is about twice that of the
 average adult brain. As we gain new experiences, neurons that are used frequently
 develop stronger connections, while those that are rarely or never used eventually
 die. The unused connections are gradually eliminated throughout childhood and
 adolescence, a process referred to as synaptic pruning. Through synaptic pruning,
 the brain can efficiently adapt to changes in the environment.

   While the brain changes a lot during early life, adult brains are still capable of
 change. This ongoing plasticity can occur as a result of learning and experience.
 Neuroplasticity depends on the “fire together, wire together” principle:  If certain
 neurons activate simultaneously,  they’ll eventually connect. Consistent practice,
  like meditating, playing a musical instrument, or learning a new language, is likely
 to alter your brain by forming new neural pathways. This is why putting in effort
 over an extended period of time leads to an improvement in ability.

   Moreover, knowing about neuroplasticity can enhance an individual’s motivation
 and learning abilities. According to a 2009 study by psychologist Richard Nisbett,
 students who were informed about the brain’s capacity to change did better on

  These days, many teenagers skip breakfast because they are too busy or want to

sleep longer. However, this habit can seriously affect their health and concentration.

According to the concept of a food rule, we should eat based on what our body needs,

not just what is convenient or what others around us do. Our body needs energy in

the morning to function properly, especially during school hours. Skipping breakfast

often leads to fatigue, poor focus in class, and unhealthy snacking later in the day.

Even though some students may say they don’t feel hungry in the morning, this might

be due to habit, not actual health needs. By following a healthy food rule — such as

eating a balanced breakfast with carbohydrates, protein, and fruits — we can support

our brain function and stay more active throughout the day. Therefore, teenagers

should break the habit of skipping breakfast and make choices that respect their body’s

real needs. (158 words)

    service accessibility and satisfaction through public–private cooperation.
③ Finland focuses on personal choice and  flexibility, while Korea mostly relies on
    uniform, government-centered services, which can result in a mismatch between

  The  following  passage  presents two  different  cases  of  competition — the
rock–paper–scissors game and a lizard’s mating behavior. Based on these cases,
explain the main idea of the passage by describing what these two cases reveal
